targetTexts.1: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
targetTexts.2: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
targetTexts.3: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
targetTexts.4: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
targetTexts.5: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
targetTexts.6: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
targetTexts.7: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
targetTexts.8: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
targetTexts.9: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
targetTexts.10: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
targetTexts.11: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
targetTexts.12: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
targetTexts.13: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
targetTexts.14: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
targetTexts.15: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
targetTexts.16: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
targetTexts.17: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
targetTexts.18: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
targetTexts.19: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
targetTexts.20: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
targetTexts.21: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
targetTexts.22: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
targetTexts.23: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
targetTexts.24: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
targetTexts.25: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar, the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
targetTexts.26: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
targetTexts.27: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
targetTexts.28: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
targetTexts.29: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
targetTexts.30: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
